title: DTCC Director and Co-Director receive Areas of Advance Award 2026
abstract: Director Anders Logg and Co-Director Minna Karstunen have received the 2026 Areas of Advance Award from Chalmers University of Technology for their work with the Digital Twin Cities Centre.
summary: Director Anders Logg and Co-Director Minna Karstunen have received the 2026 Areas of Advance Award from Chalmers University of Technology for their work with the Digital Twin Cities Centre.
intro: Director Anders Logg and Co-Director Minna Karstunen have received the 2026 Areas of Advance Award from Chalmers University of Technology for their work with the Digital Twin Cities Centre.
body:
The Areas of Advance Award, presented since 2010 at Chalmers, has been awarded Anders Logg and Minna Karstunen for their work with Digital Twin Cities Centre. The award recognises research at Chalmers that, through cross-disciplinary collaboration, contributes to solving major challenges of the future and promotes a sustainable society.

DTCC has strengthened Sweden’s position in an emerging international field while laying the foundation for better-informed, more transparent and more sustainable decision-making in urban development, reads part of the award citation.

"It’s a great honour to receive this recognition from Chalmers for all our hard work with DTCC. We have a great team, great researchers and partners, so this award is for everyone involved. We are very motivated to keep working and developing the digital twin concept through our projects and in collaboration with academia, municipalities and the industry", says Anders Logg, Director of DTCC.

"I’m very proud that Chalmers chose to recognize DTCC through this award. We’ve come a long way since the start, and thanks to our many engaged partners and skilled researchers, we’ve had some great results. I’m looking forward to continuing working towards making city planning and construction smarter and more sustainable", says Minna Karstunen, Co-Director of DTCC.

The award is worth SEK 100,000 and is to be used for joint activities.

Read more here: https://www.chalmers.se/en/current/news/area-of-advance-award-2026-awarded-for-digital-twins-that-bring-research-and-practice-together/

**Award citation**

“Anders Logg and Minna Karstunen receive the 2026 Areas of Advance Award for developing new ways of bringing together research, technology and practice to support the sustainable urban development of the future.

Together, the two award recipients have driven the establishment and development of the Digital Twin Cities Centre, helping it achieve a strong international position. The Digital Twin Cities Centre is a platform that contributes to addressing some of the most complex societal challenges of our time. In a short period, the centre has developed an approach in which advanced modelling, data analysis and visualisation create new opportunities to understand and plan the cities of the future.

At a time when sustainability, resource use and societal development are becoming increasingly interconnected, DTCC has demonstrated how multidisciplinary research can be translated into practical benefits. By bringing together stakeholders from academia, the public sector and industry around a shared infrastructure, the centre has created the conditions for new forms of knowledge development and decision support. By combining long-term research with practical applications, DTCC has strengthened Sweden’s position in an emerging international field while laying the foundation for better-informed, more transparent and more sustainable decision-making in urban development.”
